title: Ravens' Lamar Jackson Limited, Jets' Breece Hall Out: NFL Week 7 Injury Report Highlights CBS Sports
body:
The NFL’s Week 7 slate is already shaping up as a study in how injuries can tilt the balance of power early in the season. Baltimore’s quarterback Lamar Jackson entered the Thursday night matchup against the New York Jets on a limited practice schedule, while the Jets’ dynamic rookie running back Breece Hall was listed as a non‑participant for the same game. Both absences underscore the fine line teams walk between managing health and maintaining competitive momentum as the league hurtles toward the mid‑season stretch.

Jackson’s situation is a direct result of a lingering ankle sprain that has kept him out of full‑speed drills for the past two weeks. The Ravens’ medical staff cleared him for “limited participation,” a designation that allows him to attend meetings and run a light walk‑through but restricts any high‑impact activity. Head coach John Harbaugh emphasized that the team will not rush the star quarterback back to full speed, noting that “the long‑term health of our leader is more important than a single game plan.” While Jackson’s presence on the sideline may still provide a morale boost and enable him to study the Jets’ defensive schemes, the Ravens will likely rely more heavily on backup quarterback Tyler Brock to execute the offensive game plan on Thursday.

On the other side of the field, the Jets are coping with the loss of Breece Hall, who suffered a Grade‑II hamstring strain during the previous week’s practice. The injury forced the team to place Hall on the non‑participant list, meaning he will not dress or play in the Thursday contest. Jets’ offensive coordinator Nathan Miller disclosed that the team will lean on veteran running back Michael Carter and the emerging talent of rookie running back Jalen Miller to fill the void. “Hall is a big part of our identity on offense, but we have depth. We’ll adjust our play‑calling to keep the defense honest,” Miller said, hinting at a greater reliance on short‑yard passing and screen routes to compensate for the missing power runner.

The ripple effects of these injuries extend beyond the immediate matchup. Baltimore’s defense, which has been among the league’s most aggressive units, may feel added pressure to generate turnovers and keep the Jets’ offense off the field, especially if Jackson’s mobility is curtailed. Conversely, New York’s secondary, already tested by the Patriots’ aerial assault earlier in the week, now faces the prospect of defending against a Ravens offense that could lean on its robust running game and tight‑end usage to offset any quarterback limitations.

Both teams also have broader strategic considerations. The Ravens are perched near the top of the AFC North and cannot afford a slip‑up that could jeopardize a playoff berth. Their approach to Jackson’s usage reflects a cautious optimism: protect the franchise quarterback while still fielding a competitive offense. For the Jets, who are still finding their identity under rookie head coach Mike Gordon, the loss of Hall is a setback in a season that has already seen a revolving door at the running back position. Their ability to adapt will be a litmus test for Gordon’s offensive schematics and the depth of his roster.

Looking ahead, the Week 7 injury report foreshadows a pivotal juncture for both franchises. If Jackson can return to full health and demonstrate his dual‑threat capability, Baltimore could solidify its status as a perennial contender. Meanwhile, the Jets must find a way to sustain offensive production without Hall, a challenge that could either expose a lack of depth or reveal hidden gems in the backfield. As the season progresses, the management of these injuries will likely influence not just the outcome of Thursday’s game but also each team’s trajectory toward the postseason.
